# search-research

A research page on the 2026 frontier of corpus search and tagging — for a
~30k-doc personal corpus of transcripts, internal memos, and Slack
messages. Local-first bias, opinionated, all sources cited.

## live url

- part i — search & tagging:  https://dmarzzz.github.io/search-research/
- part ii — agent harnesses:  https://dmarzzz.github.io/search-research/harnesses.html
- repo:                       https://github.com/dmarzzz/search-research
- this file:                  https://dmarzzz.github.io/search-research/llms.txt

## what to read first

- `index.html` — the full research page, also at the live url above
- `agents.json` — production-agent stack table (Goose, Claude Code, Hermes,
  Honcho, Letta, Mem0, Zep, Cognee, LangGraph, Dust)
- `papers.json` — frontier paper bibliography by area (embedding, RAG,
  tagging, evaluation, memory)
- `stacks.json` — corpus-size keyed stack recommendations (1k / 30k / 1M / 100M)
- `harnesses.json` — agent runtime characteristics: Claude Code, Goose,
  Hermes, Cursor, Cline, Continue.dev, Letta, Open Interpreter, Open
  WebUI, Aider — compared on loop / context / state / MCP / models

All five are agent-fetchable. The HTML is enriched with JSON-LD describing
which dataset URLs are which, so an agent that respects `application/ld+json`
can discover the right file without parsing markup.

## the recommended stack (~30k docs, local-first)

```
corpus/                  ← markdown/txt files, source of truth
  *.md (yaml frontmatter for tags)
index.lance/             ← LanceDB single-file store (regeneratable)
config.yaml              ← embedding model + chunking choices
search.py                ← ~150 lines, exposes index() / search() / tag()
```

Four dependencies: `lancedb`, `ollama`, `pyyaml`, `click`.
Default embedding: `nomic-embed-text:v1.5` via Ollama.
Default reranker: none in v1; add `bge-reranker-v2-gemma` if measured-needed.
Tagging: BERTopic for clustering, prototype networks for k-NN, Cleanlab
for label hygiene. LLM (Haiku) only as fallback for ambiguous cases.

## key insight

The corpus folder is the source of truth. The vector index is
**regeneratable** at any time from the corpus. That single property is
what keeps the whole stack pluggable: you can swap the embedding model,
swap the vector store, swap the search frontend, all by re-running
`reindex` against the same files.

## what to skip

- 2023-style RAG pipeline (chunk → embed → store → retrieve → rerank → stuff → synthesize) — replaced by hybrid retrieval + agentic search-as-tool
- Pure long-context "stuff everything in" — RULER and Lost-in-the-Middle show 30-50% accuracy drop past 200k tokens
- Heavy frameworks (LlamaIndex, Haystack) at this scale — complexity cost > time saved
- Managed vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate) at this scale — pay-rent SaaS for capacity unused
- Multi-vector / late-interaction (ColBERT v2) — mostly displaced by single-vector + hybrid + reranker
- LLM-tagging every doc upfront — use embedding-classifier, LLM-fallback only on ambiguous (~$30 vs $300+)

## what production agents actually use

See `agents.json` for the full table. Patterns:
- No consensus on storage backend — choose by deployment shape
- Almost no one ships their own embeddings — all defer to OpenAI/Ollama
- Memory tier splits (short-term vs long-term) are real and worth copying
- Filesystem-based memory (Anthropic, Claude Code) is having a moment for
  auditability and portability — validates the "corpus as source of truth"
  approach

## frontier papers (must-read)

- arXiv:2409.04701 — Late Chunking
- arXiv:2412.15605 — Cache-Augmented Generation (CAG)
- arXiv:2501.09136 — Agentic RAG survey
- arXiv:2307.03172 — Lost in the Middle
- arXiv:2404.06654 — RULER long-context benchmark
- arXiv:2510.21440 — eRAG (utility-based eval, 50× cheaper)
- arXiv:2309.15217 — RAGAS (still SOTA in 2026)
- arXiv:2504.15965 — From Human Memory to AI Memory
- arXiv:2309.02427 — CoALA (cognitive architectures, the consolidation framing)

Full annotated list in `papers.json`.

## the next-step questions covered (sections 10-13 of index.html)

- **Exposing your corpus to agents via MCP** — minimal server is ~100 lines
  with `search()` + `get()`. Reference impls: modelcontextprotocol/servers
  (memory, filesystem, git, fetch), vurtnec/mcp-LanceDB-node.
- **Ingestion** — slackdump for Slack, Zoom AI Companion API for meetings,
  WhisperX + pyannote v4 for raw audio. No turnkey "drop your data, get a
  corpus" tool exists — bash + python glue, ~200 lines per source.
- **Evaluation without labels** — diagnostic queries (20-30 hand-crafted
  smoke tests) + synthetic queries from LLM + RAGAS or eRAG. 1-day minimum
  harness: 500 synthetic + 25 diagnostic, ~$5-20 LLM spend.
- **Personal memory frontier** — three approaches: personal RAG, memory
  layer (Mem0/Letta/Honcho/Zep), fine-tuning. For one-user, filesystem-
  based memory (Claude Code, Cursor) is winning over DB-backed. The bet
  is observability: files you can read.

## part ii — agent harnesses (harnesses.html)

Once the corpus + index + MCP server exist, the next layer is the
runtime that consumes them. Four areas:

- **Hermes Agent deep dive** — ReAct-derivative loop optimized for prompt
  cache stability. HRR (holographic) memory uses circular convolution
  for compositional retrieval — `memory ⊛ user ⊛ role ≈ writer` — not
  cosine similarity. v0.13 "Tenacity" (May 2026), 140K stars, Apache 2.0.
  Plug an MCP server via `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. Pick when you need
  cross-session learning or scheduled cron.

- **Harness comparison** — Claude Code is the clear winner for personal
  corpus + MCP (first-class MCP, plaintext state). Goose is the strong
  fully-open alternative (multi-provider, MCP reference quality). Hermes
  if memory-learning matters. Skip IDE-bound (Cursor, Cline, Continue),
  Open Interpreter (no state/MCP), Aider (code-edit centric).

- **MCP integration pitfalls** — tool-bloat curve: 5 servers ≈ 98%
  accuracy, 15 servers ≈ 35% accuracy, 15 servers + lazy-load tool search
  ≈ 91%. Practical limit: 8-12 simultaneous servers. LanceDB concurrent
  writes are dangerous (single-writer + advisory locks). The $47k/11-day
  infinite-loop case (Nov 2025) — hard budget enforcement matters.

- **Daily-driver patterns** — "personal AI as primary tool" not yet
  mainstream. Karpathy's three-layer stack (tab-complete + Claude Code
  + LLM Wiki) is the most concrete real example. Loop shapes:
  conversational, cron-driven (Hermes ships this), event-driven, autonomous
  (avoid). Trust gradient: 20% auto-approve at start → 40% by 750
  sessions. Build for halfway-there; don't wait for unified agent.

## recommended path forward

1. Build minimal MCP server (~30 lines) — covered in §10 of part i
2. Use Claude Code as daily driver — first-class MCP, plaintext state
3. Add ONE cron-driven loop for a specific task
4. Layer in dreaming-style consolidation when memory growth hurts
5. Don't pursue full autonomy — trust gradient says aim for "background
   runner" not "fully autonomous agent". Cost runaway risk is real.
